title: Protocol for constructing a hierarchical host-guest supramolecular self-assembly system in water
author: Chen, Chen, et al.
materials:
4.Preparation of the host molecule aqueous dispersion with trace amount of guest molecule.a.In a vessel, the guest molecule (for introducing host molecule in water, and addition of guest molecule is often not inferior to 0.1 equivalent of host molecule) and host molecule are dispersed with water prepared from step 3.b.The vessel with the above-mentioned aqueous dispersion is put into ultrasound equipment about 2 or 2.5 h to make sure the sufficient dispersion of the host and guest molecules.
Note:
If there is still insoluble solid in the sample, increase the temperature and prolong the ultrasonic time.

The host molecule aqueous solution or dispersion prepared in this step should be used as soon as possible to avoid the influence of precipitation on the experimental results.
CRITICAL: Hydrochloric acid is highly irritating and corrosive to eyes, skins, and the respiratory system. Handle it under a chemical fume hood, wear gloves, eye goggles and appropriate personal protective equipments.
CRITICAL: NaOH solid and NaOH aqueous solution is highly irritating and corrosive to eyes, skins, and the respiratory system. Handle it under a chemical hood wearing gloves and protective eye goggles.

steps.title: Filter water for microscopy samples
steps.instruction: Filter deionized water through a microfiltration membrane with a pore size of 220 nm before preparing samples for SEM and TEM; this step is optional but recommended for UV‑vis measurements.

steps.title: Prepare pH‑adjusted deionized water
steps.instruction: Adjust the pH of filtered deionized water to the required value using freshly prepared 1 M HCl and 1 M NaOH solutions.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 1 M HCl by diluting concentrated 12 M HCl with filtered deionized water.
Prepare 1 M NaOH by dissolving the appropriate amount of solid NaOH in filtered deionized water.
Regulate the pH of the deionized water to the desired value with the above solutions.

steps.title: Prepare deuterated solutions for NMR
steps.instruction: For NMR experiments, make the aqueous solutions with deuterated reagents such as D₂O, DCl, and NaOD instead of regular water.

steps.title: Prepare aqueous guest solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve the guest molecule CPDB in the pH‑adjusted water, optionally adding ≤1 % (v/v) organic solvent if solubility is poor, then ultrasonicate for 1–1.5 h to ensure complete dissolution; wash all vessels with filtered deionized water and dry at 25 °C before use.

substeps.instruction: Add the powdered guest molecule to a vessel containing the prepared water.
If the guest is poorly water‑soluble, add a trace amount of organic solvent (≤1 % v/v) to aid dissolution.
Ultrasonicate the mixture for 1 h or 1.5 h until fully dissolved.
Wash all vessels thoroughly with filtered deionized water and dry them at a constant temperature of 25 °C.

steps.title: Prepare aqueous host solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve the host molecule CB[8] in the pH‑adjusted water and ultrasonicate for 1–1.5 h to achieve a clear solution.

substeps.instruction: Add the host molecule to a vessel containing the prepared water.
Ultrasonicate the mixture for 1 h or 1.5 h until the host is fully dissolved.

steps.title: Prepare host dispersion with trace guest
steps.instruction: Create a dispersion containing the host molecule and a small amount of guest (≥0.1 equivalent of host) in the prepared water, then ultrasonicate for 2–2.5 h; if solids remain, increase temperature and extend sonication, and use the dispersion immediately to avoid precipitation.

substeps.instruction: Add the host molecule and the guest molecule (≥0.1 equiv relative to host) to a vessel with the prepared water.
Ultrasonicate the mixture for 2 h or 2.5 h to ensure thorough dispersion.
If insoluble material persists, raise the temperature and prolong the ultrasonic treatment.
Use the resulting dispersion promptly to prevent precipitation from affecting results.
